results.title: Increase CUDA memory with Sysmem Fallback Policy
results.content: # Increase CUDA memory with Sysmem Fallback Policy | by usamakenway | Medium. # Increase CUDA memory with Sysmem Fallback Policy. Nvidia recently released driver 536.40 which enables Sysmem Fallback Policy. This allows developers to utilize CPU RAM as overflow GPU VRAM when running out of GPU memory. The driver efficiently shares CPU RAM with GPU VRAM as one unified CUDA memory pool. This is useful for testing and development where a small VRAM boost is needed to avoid crashes, like when training large AI models that fluctuate in memory usage. For example: If my GPU VRAM is 10GB and during training allocation is reaching 9.5 GB with a certain batch size, and if it fluctuates from 9 GB to 10.5 GB. Previously, libraries like Accelerate offloaded layers to CPU and SSD when GPU memory was consumed by the help of **device_map**, but at a performance cost. In this case we get the Cuda out of memory error. Memory error with [Prefer No Sysmem Fallback]. No Memory error with [Sysmem Fallback].

Add option to disable CPU fallback when GPU memory is insufficient#10707 Add option to disable CPU fallback when GPU memory is insufficient#10707 feature request New feature or requestNew feature or request opened on May 14, 2025 · edited by seanthegeek Thanks for the awesome project — it's very fun to run local LLMs efficiently. I'd like to request a configuration option (environment variable, CLI flag, or config file setting) to **disable automatic CPU fallback** when the GPU does not have enough memory to load a model. Instead of falling back to CPU, Ollama should: * Return an error or fail fast when the model cannot fit in available GPU memory. * Optionally include a flag like `--gpu-only` or an environment variable like `OLLAMA_GPU_ONLY=true`. OLLAMA_GPU_ONLY=true ollama run llama3:70b # => Error: insufficient GPU memory, model cannot be loaded While some users restrict CPU usage externally (e.g., via Docker), it's a brittle workaround and doesn't clearly signal a failure due to GPU memory limits.
